title: Protease-catalyzed enzymatic synthesis of antifreeze peptide oligomers and their cryopreservation performance.
study_design: Protease-catalyzed synthesis of sequence isomers followed by IRI/thermal hysteresis assays and sheep RBC freeze-thaw tests.

experiments.intervention: L-PTAA oligomer at 5.0 mg/mL and higher tested concentrations
experiments.result: Only L-PTAA showed significant IRI; at 5.0 mg/mL MLGS was 7% of PBS blank and higher concentration did not add significant benefit.

experiments.cooling: −78 °C dry-ice/isopropanol slush 60 s, then dry ice 20 min
experiments.outcome_name: RBC recovery calculated as 100% minus hemolysis
experiments.result: Recovery peaked at 34% with 10 mg/mL L-PTAA; lower and higher tested doses dropped significantly. Five replicates were prepared.
experiments.sample_size: Five replicate suspensions; independent animal/donor count not specified
experiments.source_locator: Results, Cryopreservation of sheep RBCs; Figure 7; Methods

main_finding: Sequence-specific L-PTAA, but not L-PAAT/L-PATA, combined IRI activity with modest sheep-RBC recovery under a defined rapid freeze-thaw assay.
limitations: Sheep RBC transfer model; recovery is a hemolysis-derived denominator, not absolute cell yield.
The authors state precise structural origins of IRI/thermal hysteresis remain speculative; no direct biological pathway perturbation was tested.
A 1:1 mixture of 500 µL RBC suspension and 500 µL polymer solution was used; dose labels should be reconciled to final-mixture versus stock concentration before replication.
A six-day nonfreezing hemolysis test at 4 °C does not establish long-term cryostorage performance, nucleated-cell toxicity or post-thaw physiological function.
Sequence isomer controls distinguish backbone order from amino-acid composition, but polymer chain-length/lot distributions require characterization.
mechanism_claim: IRI and ice growth were directly measured; the paper attributes cryoprotection chiefly to ice modulation, while biological pathway inhibition was not tested.
reviewer: Luna extraction; root selected methods/results and interpretation review

title: Amino acid-functionalised trehalose for multifunctional cryopreservation.
cell_types: HaCaT human keratinocyte cytocompatibility model; cryopreservation-model allocation needs full text
study_design: Compound synthesis plus DSC, IRI, freeze-float, radical-scavenging, cytocompatibility, and mammalian-cell cryopreservation screening; abstract only.

experiments.outcome_name: glass transition, IRI, nucleation, radical scavenging
experiments.result: 1c had Tg up to −25 °C; diesters showed trehalose-comparable IRI, controlled elevated-subzero nucleation, and radical-scavenging activity.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: comparable ice recrystallisation inhibition (IRI) activity to trehalose

experiments.model: Mammalian cryopreservation trials; HaCaT explicitly identified for cytocompatibility, exact cryo-model allocation unverified
experiments.timepoint: multiple time points; abstract does not specify
experiments.result: Diesters showed lower cytotoxicity than DMSO/trehalose at multiple time points and measurable cryoprotection, but lower overall recovery than 10 wt% DMSO.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: despite lower overall recovery relative to 10 wt% DMSO

main_finding: The abstract supports a dual physical/chemical screening rationale and HaCaT-cell cryoprotection signal, but exact protocols and doses require full text.
limitations: Publisher page was inaccessible in the bounded pass; no concentration, loading, cooling, warming, storage, denominator, or replicate details inferred.
HaCaT cytocompatibility and radical-scavenging results do not establish a specific biological pathway mechanism.
Glass transition and acellular radical scavenging do not establish cell vitrification or direct inhibition of a cell-death pathway.
The lower-recovery result is retained; favorable toxicity alone is insufficient to rank above a demonstrated functional recovery lead.
mechanism_claim: Physical IRI/thermal and radical-scavenging assays are reported; direct biological pathway perturbation is not established.
reviewer: Luna extraction; root selected methods/results and interpretation review
